studies.title: CINRG pilot trial of coenzyme Q10 in steroid-treated Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
studies.abstract: Corticosteroid treatment slows disease progression and is the standard of care for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is a potent antioxidant that may improve function in dystrophin-deficient muscle. We performed an open-label, "add-on" pilot study of CoQ10 in thirteen 5-10-year-old DMD patients on steroids. The primary outcome measure was the total quantitative muscle testing (QMT) score. Twelve of 16 children (mean age 8.03 ± 1.64 years) completed the trial. Target serum levels of CoQ10 (≥2.5 μg/ml) were shown to be subject- and administration-dependent. Nine of 12 subjects showed an increase in total QMT score. Overall, CoQ10 treatment resulted in an 8.5% increase in muscle strength (P = 0.03). Addition of CoQ10 to prednisone therapy in DMD patients resulted in an increase in muscle strength. These results warrant a larger, controlled trial of CoQ10 in DMD.

studies.title: Case Report: Myoclonic and tremulous movements associated with COQ8A-related coenzyme Q10 deficiency type 4.
studies.abstract:
Background

Primary coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) deficiency is a rare, treatable mitochondrial disorder often caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in COQ8A gene (also known as ADCK3). It typically manifests as childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia with variable multisystem involvement. Early recognition is critical, as CoQ10 supplementation has potential to significantly alleviate clinical manifestations and modify natural progression of the disease. Here, we provide a rare phenotype of paroxysmal dyskinesias caused by compound heterozygous variants of COQ8A gene.

Case

A 21-year-old man presented with myoclonic tremor, mild dysarthria, ataxia and emotional instability. The brain MRI showed cerebellar atrophy. Biochemical workup revealed low plasma CoQ10 levels. Whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous COQ8A variants: two novel missense substitutions [NM_020247.5:c.641T>A (p.Leu214Gln), NM_020247.5:c.1621T>C (p.Ser541Pro)], each inherited from an asymptomatic parent. The patient was initiated on oral CoQ10 at a dose of 200 mg twice daily, accompanied by supportive interventions targeting emotional regulation. A marked improvement in tremor symptoms was observed shortly after treatment initiation; however, intermittent muscle tremors persisted during periods of emotional agitation. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained on CoQ10 at 300 mg twice daily and levetiracetam at 500 mg twice daily, with sustained symptom control.

Conclusion

This case highlights that COQ8A-related CoQ10 deficiency can present with serious neurological crises among young people and underscores the importance of rapid genetic diagnosis in such scenarios. Early and aggressive CoQ10 supplementation led to clinical stabilization in our patient, reinforcing that primary CoQ10 deficiency is a reversible cause of neurodegenerative disease. We emphasize genotype-phenotype diversity in COQ8A disease and the crucial need for early detection and treatment to improve prognosis. We propose that clinicians maintain a high index of suspicion for primary CoQ10 deficiency in patients presenting with unexplained dystonia or ataxia, as timely intervention may significantly improve clinical outcomes.

studies.title: Cerebellar ataxia and severe muscle CoQ10 deficiency in a patient with a novel mutation in ADCK3.
studies.abstract: Inherited ataxias are a group of heterogeneous disorders in children or adults but their genetic definition remains still undetermined in almost half of the patients. However, CoQ10 deficiency is a rare cause of cerebellar ataxia and ADCK3 is the most frequent gene associated with this defect. We herein report a 48 year old man, who presented with dysarthria and walking difficulties. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed a marked cerebellar atrophy. Serum lactate was elevated. Tissues obtained by muscle and skin biopsies were studied for biochemical and genetic characterization. Skeletal muscle biochemistry revealed decreased activities of complexes I+III and II+III and a severe reduction of CoQ10 , while skin fibroblasts showed normal CoQ10 levels. A mild loss of maximal respiration capacity was also found by high-resolution respirometry. Molecular studies identified a novel homozygous deletion (c.504del_CT) in ADCK3, causing a premature stop codon. Western blot analysis revealed marked reduction of ADCK3 protein levels. Treatment with CoQ10 was started and, after 1 year follow-up, patient neurological condition slightly improved. This report suggests the importance of investigating mitochondrial function and, in particular, muscle CoQ10 levels, in patients with adult-onset cerebellar ataxia. Moreover, clinical stabilization by CoQ10 supplementation emphasizes the importance of an early diagnosis.

studies.title: Coenzyme Q10 deficiency and isolated myopathy.
studies.abstract: Three unrelated, sporadic patients with muscle coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) deficiency presented at 32, 29, and 6 years of age with proximal muscle weakness and elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) and lactate levels, but without myoglobinuria, ataxia, or seizures. Muscle biopsy showed lipid storage myopathy, combined deficiency of respiratory chain complexes I and III, and CoQ10 levels below 50% of normal. Oral high-dose CoQ10 supplementation improved muscle strength dramatically and normalized serum CK.

studies.title: Post-workout supplementation with CoQ10 and sports drink on exercise performance and muscle recovery after exercise in normal and overweight males.
studies.abstract:
Background

Post-workout supplementation has been used in athletes and recreational exercisers; however, responses between normal and overweight individuals on exercise performance and muscle recovery are less known.

Methods

Normal and overweight young adult males (21 subjects/group) participated in resistance and fatiguing exercises before receiving post-workout supplements: placebo, coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), or sports drink in a crossover design. Resistance exercises included upper body exercise (bench press, upright row, and standing shoulder press) and lower body exercise (dead lift, back squat, and front squat) at 75% of one-repetition maximum (1 RM). Fatiguing exercise was performed on a cycle ergometer with 3 ​min of all-out effort at 3.5% of body mass. Participants consumed post-workout supplements within 10 ​min of exercise completion and repeated-bout exercise was performed 1 ​h later, followed by cardiovascular responses, urinary biomarkers, and delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) assessments.

Results

There were effects of overweight on resistance exercise volume, critical power, fatigue index, and post-exercise diastolic blood pressure (DBP). However, no differences in urinary biomarkers of muscle damage (potassium and creatinine) or DOMS between normal and overweight individuals. After supplementation, CoQ10 and sports drink increased resistance exercise volume regardless of body mass and increased critical power in the normal group. Additionally, CoQ10 supplementation was associated with a reduction in urinary biomarkers and DOMS in both groups.

Conclusion

These findings are beneficial for sport scientists, nutritionists, and exercise physiologists in guiding post-workout supplementation with CoQ10 and sports drink to improve exercise performance and muscle recovery in normal and overweight individuals.

studies.title: Assessment of CoQ10 Dietary Intake in a Mediterranean Cohort of Familial Hypercholesterolemia Patients: A Pilot Study.
studies.abstract: Coenzyme Q 10 is a lipid molecule that works as a mobile electron transporter in the mitochondrial respiratory chain and, in addition, plays the role of an antioxidant. Interestingly, CoQ10 synthesis in human cells derives from the mevalonate pathway, the same metabolic route that delivers endogenous cholesterol. Mutations leading to Familial Hypercholesterolemia (FH) alter the levels of CoQ10 production and remarkably, statin therapy associated muscular symptoms (SAMSs) might also be modulated by CoQ10 supplementation. CoQ10 is also provided by diet and only a few studies have calculated the dietary intake of this metabolite among populations. Here, we present our Spanish FH cohort ( A cohort of 75.1% followed lipid-lowering treatment at inclusion, being the most prescribed drugs statin alone (32.7%) and statins combined with ezetimibe (56.6%). The average time on statin treatment was 3.7 years. Interestingly, 22% of cohort patients presented with SAMS. In addition, we performed an exhaustive literature review to define for the first time the CoQ10 content present in food typically found in Spain or other southern-European countries and classified them from very rich (over 50 mg/kg) to very poor (<1 mg/kg). With this information, we calculated the daily intake of CoQ10 from a small group (12) of selected FH patients using a validated food-frequency questionnaire (FFQ) and determined a daily intake 9.72 ± 2.64 mg/day, different to other described populations. we discussed the relevance of exogenous CoQ10 for FH development and potential SAMS. Interestingly, this information can be extrapolated to define the regular CoQ10 intake of the Spanish population, especially when following the MedDiet.

studies.title: CoenzymeQ10 and Ischemic Preconditioning Potentially Prevent Tourniquet-Induced Ischemia/Reperfusion in Knee Arthroplasty, but Combined Pretreatment Possibly Ne
studies.abstract: Tourniquet (TQ) use during total knee arthroplasty (TKA) induces ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction. This study aims to determine the effects of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) and ischemic preconditioning (IPC), either alone or in combination, on I/R-induced mitochondrial respiration alteration in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and pain following TKA. Forty-four patients were allocated into four groups: control, CoQ10, IPC, and CoQ10 + IPC. CoQ10 dose was 300 mg/day for 28 days. IPC protocol was three cycles of 5/5-min I/R time. Mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates (OCRs) of PBMCs were measured seven times, at baseline and during ischemic/reperfusion phases, with XFe 96 extracellular flux analyzer. Postoperative pain was assessed for 48 h. CoQ10 improved baseline mitochondrial uncoupling state; however, changes in OCRs during the early phase of I/R were not significantly different from the placebo. Compared to ischemic data, IPC transiently increased basal OCR and ATP production at 2 h after reperfusion. Clinically, CoQ10 significantly decreased pain scores and morphine requirements at 24 h. CoQ10 + IPC abolished analgesic effect of CoQ10 and mitochondrial protection of IPC. In TKA with TQ, IPC enhanced mitochondrial function by a transient increase in basal and ATP-linked respiration, and CoQ10 provides postoperative analgesic effect. Surprisingly, CoQ10 + IPC interferes with beneficial effects of each intervention.

studies.title: Effects of Coenzyme Q10 on Skeletal Muscle Oxidative Metabolism in Statin Users Assessed Using <sup>31</sup>P Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy: a Randomized Cont
studies.abstract:
Objectives

Statins partially block the production of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), an essential component for mitochondrial function. Reduced skeletal muscle mitochondrial oxidative capacity has been proposed to be a cause of statin myalgia and can be measured using 31phosphorus magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS). The purpose of this study is to assess the effect of CoQ10 oral supplementation on mitochondrial function in statin users using 31P-MRS.

Design/setting

In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study, 21 adults aged 47-73 were randomized to statin+placebo (n=9) or statin+CoQ10 (n=12). Phosphocreatine (PCr) recovery kinetics of calf muscles were assessed at baseline (off statin and CoQ10) and 4 weeks after randomization to either statin+CoQ10 or statin+placebo.

Results

Baseline and post-treatment PCr recovery kinetics were assessed for 19 participants. After 4 weeks of statin+ CoQ10 or statin+placebo, the overall relative percentage change (100*(baseline-follow up)/baseline) in PCr recovery time was -15.1% compared with baseline among all participants, (p-value=0.258). Participants randomized to statin+placebo (n=9) had a relative percentage change in PCr recovery time of -18.9%, compared to -7.7% among participants (n=10) receiving statin+CoQ10 (p-value=0.448).

Conclusions

In this pilot study, there was no significant change in mitochondrial function in patients receiving 4 weeks of statin+CoQ10 oral therapy when compared to patients on statin+placebo.

studies.title: Coenzyme Q10 improves redox homeostasis, mitochondrial biogenesis, and irisin signaling in fast- and slow-twitch muscle fibers in a reserpine-induced fibromyalg
studies.abstract:
Aims

Fibromyalgia (FM) is a chronic pain syndrome frequently associated with muscular oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation in a reserpine-induced FM rat model, focusing on its effects in gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.

Materials and methods

Female Wistar rats were divided into Control, FM, CoQ10, and FM + CoQ10 groups. Reserpine (1 mg kg-1 day-1, s.c.) was administered for 3 days to induce FM; CoQ10 (150 mg kg-1 day-1, oral gavage) was given for 7 days. Cold hyperalgesia, serum TNF-α, muscular CoQ9/CoQ10 levels, oxidative stress markers (MDA, PC, TOS), antioxidant defenses (SOD, GSH, TAC), and mRNA expression of AMPK, SIRT1, PGC-1α, and FNDC5 were assessed.

Key findings

Reserpine successfully induced cold hyperalgesia and increased serum TNF-α. In both muscle types of FM rats, CoQ10 levels were depleted, oxidative damage markers were elevated, and antioxidant defenses (GSH, SOD) were compromised. CoQ10 supplementation attenuated cold hyperalgesia, normalized muscular CoQ10 (and influenced CoQ9), significantly reduced MDA, PC, and TOS levels, and partially restored GSH and SOD activity. Notably, CoQ10 robustly upregulated the mRNA expression of AMPK, SIRT1, and PGC-1α, key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis, in both gastrocnemius and soleus muscles. Furthermore, CoQ10 significantly increased the expression of FNDC5, the precursor to the myokine irisin.

Significance

These findings suggest that CoQ10 ameliorates reserpine-induced FM-like pathology by mitigating oxidative stress, enhancing antioxidant capacity, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis, and stimulating the FNDC5/irisin pathway in skeletal muscle, highlighting its multifaceted therapeutic potential for FM.

studies.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evidence of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid for mitochondrial COQ2 deficiency.
studies.abstract: Primary coenzyme Q (CoQ) deficiency is a mitochondrial disorder with variable clinical presentation and limited response to standard CoQ10 supplementation. Recent studies suggest that 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (4-HBA), a biosynthetic precursor of CoQ, may serve as a substrate enhancement treatment in cases caused by pathogenic variants in COQ2, a gene encoding a key enzyme in CoQ biosynthesis. However, it remains unclear whether 4-HBA is required throughout life to maintain health, whether it offers advantages over CoQ10 treatment, and whether these findings are translatable to humans. Here, we demonstrate that lifelong 4-HBA supplementation in a murine model carrying the pathogenic Coq2A252V variant is well tolerated and prevents the onset of mitochondrial encephalopathy. In contrast, withdrawal of 4-HBA leads to progressive neurological decline. Notably, while conventional CoQ10 supplementation transiently ameliorated cardiac dysfunction, it failed to prevent fatal neurological deterioration. Guided by these preclinical findings, we initiated a first-in-human individual therapeutic trial with 4-HBA in a 3-year-old boy with genetically confirmed primary CoQ10 deficiency due to compound heterozygous pathogenic COQ2 variants. The patient presented with a Leigh-like syndrome characterized by bilateral brain lesions, developmental delay, muscular hypotonia, failure to thrive, lactic acidosis and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Despite high-dose oral CoQ10 supplementation, clinical response had been minimal. Prior to clinical application, patient-derived fibroblasts were treated in vitro with 4-HBA, resulting in a marked increase in endogenous CoQ10 levels. Following the initiation of oral 4-HBA treatment, the patient experienced rapid and sustained remission of proteinuria, improved renal hyperfiltration and a gradual increase in serum CoQ10 concentrations. No adverse effects were observed during a 6-month follow-up. Clinically, the patient showed notable improvements in motor skills, language acquisition, cognitive alertness and overall development, accompanied by significant gains in growth and nutritional status. Clinical recovery was also reflected by improved scores on the Newcastle Paediatric Mitochondrial Disease Scale. These findings support 4-HBA as a promising targeted metabolic treatment for COQ2-related CoQ deficiency and highlight the need for further clinical investigation.

studies.title: Involvement of the PINK1/PARKIN pathway in enhancing mitochondrial function and mitophagy in reserpine-induced fibromyalgia mice through strength exercise and c
studies.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the impact of reserpine-induced fibromyalgia and evaluate the potential effects of resistance exercise or CoQ10 administration on muscle strength, structure, and expression of mitochondrial markers in adult mice. Central to this investigation is an exploration of the molecular mechanisms underlying mitophagy via the PINK1/Parkin pathway.

Methods

This study sought to elucidate the Impact of 4 weeks of either climbing exercise or coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation (10 mg/kg, administered once daily) on skeletal muscle and mitochondrial functions within a reserpine-induced fibromyalgia (FM) mouse model. Evaluation encompassed the assessment of key mitochondrial markers, including PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1), PARKIN, Mitofusion2, cytochrome c oxidase, citrate synthase, and fibronectin type III domain-containing protein 5 (FNDC5), alongside morphological examinations of the gastrocnemius muscle.

Results

Climbing exercise significantly improved fibromyalgia (FM)-like symptoms and enhanced the expression of mitochondrial marker genes in the gastrocnemius muscle. Histological and ultra-structural studies showed nearly normal muscle fiber structure, banding patterns, mitochondria shape and size, and a notable reduction in collagen fibrosis compared to FM. CoQ10 supplementation also improved mitochondrial gene expression but did not significantly affect FNDC gene expression. Ultrastructural analysis revealed mostly normal muscle fibers with regular banding, though some areas showed disturbances with multiple sub-sarcolemmal and interfibrillar mitochondria.

Conclusion

This study underscores the efficacy of both resistance exercise and CoQ10 supplementation as viable strategies for improving FM-related symptoms and enhancing mitochondrial function in mice.

studies.title: Comparing the efficacy of concomitant treatment of resistance exercise and creatine monohydrate versus multiple individual therapies in age related sarcopenia.
studies.abstract: Aging-related sarcopenia is a degenerative loss of strength and skeletal muscle mass that impairs quality of life. Evaluating NUDT3 gene and myogenin expression as new diagnostic tools in sarcopenia. Also, comparing the concomitant treatment of resistance exercise (EX) and creatine monohydrate (CrM) versus single therapy by EX, coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), and CrM using aged rats. Sixty male rats were equally divided into groups. The control group, aging group, EX-treated group, the CoQ10 group were administered (500 mg/kg) of CoQ10, the CrM group supplied (0.3 mg/kg of CrM), and a group of CrM concomitant with resistance exercise. Serum lipid profiles, certain antioxidant markers, electromyography (EMG), nudix hydrolase 3 (NUDT3) expression, creatine kinase (CK), and sarcopenic index markers were measured after 12 weeks. The gastrocnemius muscle was stained with hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) and myogenin. The EX-CrM combination showed significant improvement in serum lipid profile, antioxidant markers, EMG, NUDT3 gene, myogenin expression, CK, and sarcopenic index markers from other groups. The NUDT3 gene and myogenin expression have proven efficient as diagnostic tools for sarcopenia. Concomitant treatment of CrM and EX is preferable to individual therapy because it reduces inflammation, improves the lipid serum profile, promotes muscle regeneration, and thus has the potential to improve sarcopenia.

studies.title: Coenzyme Q10 supplementation acts as antioxidant on dystrophic muscle cells.
studies.abstract: Increased oxidative stress is a frequent feature in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). High reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, associated with altered enzyme antioxidant activity, have been reported in dystrophic patients and mdx mice, an experimental model of DMD. In this study, we investigated the effects of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) on oxidative stress marker levels and calcium concentration in primary cultures of dystrophic muscle cells from mdx mice. Primary cultures of skeletal muscle cells from C57BL/10 and mdx mice were treated with coenzyme Q10 (5 μM) for 24 h. The untreated mdx and C57BL/10 muscle cells were used as controls. The MTT and live/dead cell assays showed that CoQ10 presented no cytotoxic effect on normal and dystrophic muscle cells. Intracellular calcium concentration, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> production, 4-HNE, and SOD-2 levels were higher in mdx muscle cells. This study demonstrated that CoQ10 treatment was able to reduce levels of oxidative stress markers, such as H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, acting as an antioxidant, as well as decreasing abnormal intracellular calcium influx in dystrophic muscles cells. explanation.what_it_is_line: Fat-soluble molecule that cells use to generate energy; found in all living things.
explanation.what_it_is: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10, also called ubiquinone or ubidecarenone) is a small fat-soluble molecule your cells naturally produce. It lives primarily in the energy-generating structures inside cells called mitochondria — think of it as a worker on an assembly line that helps convert the food you eat into usable energy (ATP, the currency your cells spend for work). Your body makes less CoQ10 as you age, and certain medications, especially statins (which lower cholesterol), can lower your levels further. It's available as an oral supplement in capsules or tablets, typically derived from fermentation or chemical synthesis.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Shuttles electrons in cell energy production; protects cells from oxidative damage.
explanation.how_it_works: CoQ10 works in two main ways. First, it acts as an electron shuttle in the mitochondrial energy pipeline — it ferries electrons between protein complexes, a critical step that allows your cells to efficiently generate ATP (the energy molecule they burn for every task). Second, it's a potent antioxidant, meaning it neutralizes harmful byproducts (called free radicals) that accumulate during energy production and can damage cell membranes and DNA if left unchecked. This dual role — energy production plus cellular protection — may explain why it affects so many health outcomes. Because CoQ10 is highly fat-soluble (XLogP 19.4, meaning it strongly prefers fatty environments), it embeds itself in the fatty membranes that wrap your cells and mitochondria, where it's positioned to do its work.
explanation.safety_line: Generally well-tolerated in short-term trials; long-term safety and drug interactions not well studied.
explanation.safety_detail: The retrieved trials — mostly 4–12 weeks in duration — reported few or mild side effects (gastrointestinal upset being most common); no serious adverse events were attributed to CoQ10 in the studies provided. However, all trials were short, none assessed long-term exposure (months to years), and most enrolled narrow populations (e.g., statin-treated patients, athletes, specific disease groups). The true safety profile in diverse populations and over longer durations remains unknown.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety: no trials >12 weeks retrieved; extended use in the general population is untested.
Drug interactions: CoQ10 is highly lipophilic and may interact with medications or other supplements that rely on fat absorption; not adequately studied in retrieved trials.
Excluded or underrepresented populations: no trials in pregnancy, adolescents, or severe kidney/liver disease; safety in these groups is unknown.
Statin interactions: some evidence suggests CoQ10 may mitigate statin-induced muscle symptoms, but the mechanism and optimal dosing strategy remain unclear.
explanation.chem_meaning: CoQ10 is a large, highly lipophilic (fat-loving) molecule with a long hydrocarbon tail (10 isoprene units in the decamethyltetraconta backbone) and a quinone head-group. Its extreme lipophilicity (XLogP 19.4) means it dissolves poorly in water but readily embeds in fatty cell membranes and mitochondrial cristae, where its biochemical work occurs — this is why oral absorption depends on dietary fat and why formulation (powder vs. ubiquinone vs. ubiquinol) affects bioavailability.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converged on a cardiovascular benefit, with a pooled effect of a 0.96-unit reduction in a composite cardiovascular risk score (95% CI: −1.88 to −0.03). Human evidence dominates (16 human trials vs. 10 animal studies out of 26 total); verified participant count across 6 trials was ~3,364, though most abstracts omitted sample sizes, so the true total is substantially larger. Studies ranged from 2016–2025 and included statin-treated patients, burn patients, soccer players, and those with prediabetes/type 2 diabetes, with durations typically 4–12 weeks.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong human evidence (16 trials) with independent replication of findings across 4 separate meta-analyses, plus adequately powered pooled analyses, meets the threshold for Strong. Cardiovascular outcomes are directly measured and clinically relevant.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six human trials and two animal studies examined lipid profiles. A meta-analysis of 2,794 participants found CoQ10 supplementation reduced LDL cholesterol and triglycerides in adults, and a 2026 cardiovascular meta-analysis included lipid markers in prediabetes/type 2 diabetes populations. Individual RCTs (n=30–104) in hypertensive, hypercholesterolemic, and metabolic syndrome patients showed improvements in lipid profiles. One observational study assessed dietary CoQ10 intake in familial hypercholesterolemia. Verified participant count across 3 studies was ~2,928, with most trials 4–12 weeks in duration.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate: only 3 primary human RCTs and 2 pooled analyses retrieved — below the number required for Strong. Evidence exists and is human-based, but the synthesis is smaller and less independently replicated than cardiovascular outcomes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converged on an anti-inflammatory effect, with a pooled mean reduction of 0.45 units in inflammatory markers (95% CI: −0.67 to −0.24). Human trials dominate the evidence (16 human vs. 22 animal studies out of 38 total). Verified participant count across 7 trials was ~2,125, though most abstracts omitted sizes. A 2023 meta-analysis of 1,517 participants assessed optimal dosing; a 2020 review pooled oxidative stress parameters; a 2017 review (n=428) examined inflammatory markers. Recent studies (2023–2026) included juvenile idiopathic arthritis (n=58) and various chronic disease populations, with typical durations of 4–12 weeks.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong: 16 human trials with independently replicated findings across 5 meta-analyses, adequately powered pooled estimates, and direct measurement of inflammatory biomarkers (e.g., CRP, TNF-α, IL-6) meet the criteria for Strong.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Nineteen human trials and 5 animal studies examined muscle strength and physical function. A 2023 scoping review synthesized evidence on CoQ10 for sarcopenia, frailty, and falls. Individual RCTs included small samples: n=10–38 participants with multiple sclerosis, high-intensity training adaptations, chronic kidney disease, and statin-treated patients. A 2022 RCT (n=37) was double-blinded placebo-controlled in statin users; a 2023 RCT (n=25) was a crossover design; most durations were 8 weeks or less. Verified participant count across 8 trials was ~284.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate: 19 human trials exist, but only a single meta-analysis/systematic review was retrieved, and it has not been independently replicated — the consistency criterion for Strong is not met. Small sample sizes and short durations limit precision.

explanation.evidence_base: CoQ10 has been extensively studied, with 26–38 trials retrieved per outcome. Human evidence predominates (16 human trials for cardiovascular and inflammation; 19 for muscle strength), supported by animal mechanistic studies. Most trials are RCTs ranging from 2016–2026, typically 4–12 weeks in duration, conducted in disease or aging populations (statin-treated patients, diabetes, arthritis, athletes). Four independent meta-analyses converge on cardiovascular and inflammation outcomes, lending credibility; lipids and muscle strength are supported by smaller or less-replicated syntheses. The recency and breadth of human RCTs is a strength; the brevity of follow-up (≤12 weeks) and the exclusion of many populations (healthy young adults, pregnancy, severe organ disease) limit what we know about long-term efficacy and broader applicability.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided show no long-term trials (>12 weeks) — whether benefits persist or accumulate over months is unknown. Optimal dosing varies across studies (50–600 mg/day retrieved), but the records show only one analysis explicitly addressing dose–response. Populations in the retrieved trials skew toward older, disease-afflicted, or athletic cohorts; efficacy in healthy young adults or children is not represented in the sample. The mechanism of lipid lowering appears less consistent across studies than cardiovascular or inflammatory outcomes, suggesting moderating factors (diet, baseline lipids, dosage, formulation) that the records do not clearly delineate.

appraisal.headline: CoQ10 shows consistent but modest effects on cardiovascular and inflammatory biomarkers in retrieved trials; the evidence base is substantially incomplete (most studies omit sample sizes), and clinical meaningfulness of the pooled effects remains unclear.

concerns.issue: Massive missing data on sample sizes
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes, only 24 of 96 total studies (25%) report sample sizes in the abstracts. For cardiovascular (Strong grade), only 6 of 26 studies report n; for inflammation (Strong grade), only 7 of 38 studies report n. The engine estimates true participant totals are 'substantially larger,' but this opacity means effect size stability cannot be independently verified and a single large unreported trial could materially shift pooled estimates.

The inflammation outcome (graded Strong) includes 22 of 38 studies (58%) in animal models, yet the pooled effect [-0.45 CI: -0.67 to -0.24] is presented as supporting human clinical utility. Animal models of inflammation often show larger effect sizes than human trials; the 16 human studies alone may not support the Same strength of inference drawn from the combined set.

The cardiovascular outcome (Strong grade) pools studies on statin-induced myopathy, cardiac stress in athletes, burn patients, prediabetes, exercise performance, and lipid profiles—distinct pathophysiologies and endpoints. The pooled mean difference of -0.96 [-1.88 to -0.03] has a 95% CI that barely excludes zero and is computed across fundamentally incomparable clinical scenarios, raising questions about whether the pooled estimate reflects any single actionable clinical claim.

concerns.issue: Cholesterol/lipids graded Moderate with minimal evidence
concerns.detail: Only 8 studies total with 3 reporting sample sizes (n=30, 104, 2794); the 2794-participant meta-analysis is listed but no pooled effect is extractable from the abstracts provided. The engine explicitly notes this outcome is 'below the threshold for the top tier' due to limited human evidence, yet cardiovascular receives a Strong grade despite overlapping populations and similar methodological constraints.

concerns.issue: Muscle strength evidence is small and fragmented
concerns.detail: Eight of 24 muscle strength studies report sample sizes; six of those eight enrolled ≤38 participants, and the largest (n=120) is from 2015. No meta-analysis conclusion is independently replicated (single systematic review only). The median n across reported studies is 25, meaning confidence intervals are wide and heterogeneity from small-trial bias is plausible.

appraisal.mechanism_check: CoQ10 is a well-established mitochondrial electron transport cofactor, and in vitro evidence supports roles in oxidative stress and inflammation. However, the retrieved evidence does not address systemic bioavailability or tissue penetration adequately—the 2020 bioavailability trial is included but its findings are not synthesized into claims about whether oral CoQ10 reaches heart or muscle in therapeutic concentrations. The leap from biomarker reduction (CRP, TNF-α, lipid indices) to clinically meaningful improvement in cardiovascular events or functional muscle strength is substantial and not bridged by mechanistic data in these records.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that five of the six cardiovascular RCTs (2018–2025) are recent and include substantial heterogeneity in populations and dose; older meta-analyses and observational studies may reflect publication bias or inadequate blinding. The inflammation outcome, graded Strong, is driven by a 5-meta-analysis consensus, but four of five meta-analyses are from 2017–2023 and explicitly include animal data; if the human-only subset shows inconsistency or smaller effect sizes, the claim of adequately powered replication crumbles. Most critically, the pooled cardiovascular effect is -0.96 with a CI spanning zero to -1.88—if interpreted conservatively, the lower bound is clinically trivial (−0.03), and the point estimate could easily be noise in a small-trial meta-analysis.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A large (n≥500), adequately powered RCT with a pre-specified clinical outcome (e.g., cardiovascular event reduction, muscle function by standardized measures in a single disease population) and explicit reporting of blinding, allocation concealment, and attrition would establish whether biomarker improvements translate to patient-relevant benefit. Alternatively, a systematic review that separately pools human RCTs only, stratifies by population and outcome, and quantifies heterogeneity would clarify whether the Strong grades are supported by human evidence alone or inflated by animal data.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Molécula soluble en grasa que las células utilizan para generar energía; se encuentra en todos los seres vivos.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La coenzima Q10 (CoQ10, también llamada ubiquinona o ubidecarenona) es una pequeña molécula soluble en grasa que tus células producen naturalmente. Se localiza principalmente en las estructuras generadoras de energía dentro de las células llamadas mitocondrias — piénsalo como un trabajador en una línea de ensamblaje que ayuda a convertir la comida que comes en energía utilizable (ATP, la moneda que tus células gastan para trabajar). Tu cuerpo produce menos CoQ10 conforme envejeces, y ciertos medicamentos, especialmente las estatinas (que bajan el colesterol), pueden disminuir tus niveles aún más. Está disponible como suplemento oral en cápsulas o tabletas, típicamente derivado de fermentación o síntesis química.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Transporta electrones en la producción de energía celular; protege las células del daño oxidativo.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La CoQ10 funciona de dos formas principales. Primero, actúa como un transportador de electrones en el sistema de energía mitocondrial — transporta electrones entre complejos proteicos, un paso crítico que permite a tus células generar ATP eficientemente (la molécula de energía que queman para cada tarea). Segundo, es un antioxidante potente, lo que significa que neutraliza subproductos dañinos (llamados radicales libres) que se acumulan durante la producción de energía y pueden dañar membranas celulares y ADN si no se controlan. Este doble papel — producción de energía más protección celular — puede explicar por qué afecta tantos resultados de salud. Debido a que la CoQ10 es altamente soluble en grasa (XLogP 19.4, lo que significa que prefiere fuertemente ambientes grasosos), se incrusta en las membranas grasosas que envuelven tus células y mitocondrias, donde está posicionada para hacer su trabajo.
explanation_es.safety_line: Generalmente bien tolerada en ensayos a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo e interacciones farmacológicas no están bien estudiadas.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados — mayormente de 4–12 semanas de duración — reportaron pocos o leves efectos secundarios (malestar gastrointestinal siendo el más común); no se atribuyeron eventos adversos graves a la CoQ10 en los estudios proporcionados. Sin embargo, todos los ensayos fueron cortos, ninguno evaluó exposición a largo plazo (meses a años), y la mayoría incluyó poblaciones estrechas (p. ej., pacientes tratados con estatinas, atletas, grupos de enfermedades específicas). El verdadero perfil de seguridad en poblaciones diversas y durante duraciones más largas sigue siendo desconocido.
safety_bullets: Seguridad a largo plazo: sin ensayos >12 semanas recuperados; el uso extendido en la población general no ha sido probado.

Interacciones farmacológicas: la CoQ10 es altamente lipofílica y puede interactuar con medicamentos u otros suplementos que dependen de la absorción de grasa; no está adecuadamente estudiado en los ensayos recuperados.
Poblaciones excluidas o subrepresentadas: sin ensayos en embarazo, adolescentes, o enfermedad renal/hepática grave; la seguridad en estos grupos es desconocida.

Interacciones con estatinas: hay algunas evidencias que sugieren que la CoQ10 puede mitigar síntomas musculares inducidos por estatinas, pero el mecanismo y la estrategia de dosificación óptima siguen siendo poco claros.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La CoQ10 es una molécula grande, altamente lipofílica (que ama la grasa) con una larga cola de hidrocarburo (10 unidades de isopreno en la columna vertebral de decametiltetraconta) y un grupo cabeza de quinona. Su lipofilia extrema (XLogP 19.4) significa que se disuelve mal en agua pero se incrusta fácilmente en membranas celulares grasosas y crestas mitocondriales, donde ocurre su trabajo bioquímico — esta es la razón por la que la absorción oral depende de grasa dietética y por la que la formulación (polvo vs. ubiquinona vs. ubiquinol) afecta la biodisponibilidad.

La evidencia humana domina (16 ensayos humanos vs. 10 estudios en animales de 26 totales); el conteo de participantes verificado en 6 ensayos fue ~3,364, aunque la mayoría de resúmenes omitieron tamaños de muestra, por lo que el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor. Los estudios abarcaron 2016–2025 e incluyeron pacientes tratados con estatinas, pacientes con quemaduras, jugadores de fútbol, y aquellos con prediabetes/diabetes tipo 2, con duraciones típicamente de 4–12 semanas.

Los resultados cardiovasculares se miden directamente y son clínicamente relevantes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis ensayos humanos y dos estudios en animales examinaron perfiles lipídicos. Un metanálisis de 2,794 participantes encontró que la suplementación con CoQ10 redujo el colesterol LDL y triglicéridos en adultos, y un metanálisis cardiovascular de 2026 incluyó marcadores lipídicos en poblaciones con prediabetes/diabetes tipo 2. Los ECA individuales (n=30–104) en pacientes hipertensos, hipercolesterolémicos, y con síndrome metabólico mostraron mejoras en perfiles lipídicos. Un estudio observacional evaluó la ingesta dietética de CoQ10 en hipercolesterolemia familiar. El conteo de participantes verificado en 3 estudios fue ~2,928, con la mayoría de ensayos de 4–12 semanas de duración.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderada: solo 3 ECA humanos primarios y 2 análisis agrupados recuperados — por debajo del número requerido para Fuerte. La evidencia existe y está basada en humanos, pero la síntesis es menor y menos replicada independientemente que los resultados cardiovasculares.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas convergieron en un efecto antiinflamatorio, con una reducción media agrupada de 0.45 unidades en marcadores inflamatorios (IC 95%: −0.67 a −0.24). Los ensayos humanos dominan la evidencia (16 humanos vs. 22 estudios en animales de 38 totales). El conteo de participantes verificado en 7 ensayos fue ~2,125, aunque la mayoría de resúmenes omitieron tamaños. Un metanálisis de 2023 de 1,517 participantes evaluó dosificación óptima; una revisión de 2020 agrupó parámetros de estrés oxidativo; una revisión de 2017 (n=428) examinó marcadores inflamatorios. outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Fuerte: 16 ensayos humanos con hallazgos replicados independientemente en 5 metanálisis, estimados agrupados adecuadamente potenciados, y medición directa de biomarcadores inflamatorios (p. ej., PCR, TNF-α, IL-6) cumplen los criterios para Fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Diecinueve ensayos humanos y 5 estudios en animales examinaron la fuerza muscular y la función física. Una revisión de alcance de 2023 sintetizó evidencia sobre CoQ10 para sarcopenia, fragilidad, y caídas. Los ECA individuales incluyeron muestras pequeñas: n=10–38 participantes con esclerosis múltiple, adaptaciones de entrenamiento de alta intensidad, enfermedad renal crónica, y pacientes tratados con estatinas. Un ECA de 2022 (n=37) fue doble ciego controlado con placebo en usuarios de estatinas; un ECA de 2023 (n=25) fue un diseño cruzado; la mayoría de duraciones fueron de 8 semanas o menos. El conteo de participantes verificado en 8 ensayos fue ~284.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderada: existen 19 ensayos humanos, pero solo se recuperó un único metanálisis/revisión sistemática, y no ha sido replicado independientemente — el criterio de consistencia para Fuerte no se cumple. Los tamaños de muestra pequeños y duraciones cortas limitan la precisión.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La CoQ10 ha sido ampliamente estudiada, con 26–38 ensayos recuperados por resultado. La evidencia humana predomina (16 ensayos humanos para cardiovascular e inflamación; 19 para fuerza muscular), apoyada por estudios mecanísticos en animales. La mayoría de ensayos son ECA que abarcan 2016–2026, típicamente de 4–12 semanas de duración, conducidos en poblaciones de enfermedad o envejecimiento (pacientes tratados con estatinas, diabetes, artritis, atletas). Cuatro metanálisis independientes convergen en resultados cardiovasculares e inflamatorios, lo que aumenta la credibilidad; lípidos y fuerza muscular están apoyados por síntesis más pequeñas o menos replicadas. La actualidad y amplitud de los ECA humanos es una fortaleza; la brevedad del seguimiento (≤12 semanas) y la exclusión de muchas poblaciones (adultos jóvenes sanos, embarazo, enfermedad orgánica grave) limitan lo que sabemos sobre la eficacia a largo plazo y la aplicabilidad más amplia.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no muestran ensayos a largo plazo (>12 semanas) — si los beneficios persisten o se acumulan durante meses es desconocido. La dosificación óptima varía entre estudios (50–600 mg/día recuperados), pero los registros muestran solo un análisis que se enfoca explícitamente en respuesta a dosis. Las poblaciones en los ensayos recuperados se sesguen hacia cohortes mayores, afligidas por enfermedades, o atléticas; la eficacia en adultos jóvenes sanos o niños no está representada en la muestra. El mecanismo de reducción de lípidos parece menos consistente en todos los estudios que los resultados cardiovasculares o inflamatorios, sugiriendo factores moderadores (dieta, lípidos basales, dosaje, formulación) que los registros no delinean claramente.

appraisal_es.headline: CoQ10 muestra efectos consistentes pero modestos en biomarcadores cardiovasculares e inflamatorios en los ensayos recuperados; la base de evidencia es sustancialmente incompleta (la mayoría de los estudios omiten tamaños de muestra), y la relevancia clínica de los efectos agrupados sigue siendo poco clara.

concerns.issue: Datos faltantes masivos sobre tamaños de muestra
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados, solo 24 de 96 estudios totales (25%) reportan tamaños de muestra en los resúmenes. Para cardiovascular (grado Fuerte), solo 6 de 26 estudios reportan n; para inflamación (grado Fuerte), solo 7 de 38 estudios reportan n. El motor estima que los totales verdaderos de participantes son 'sustancialmente mayores', pero esta falta de transparencia significa que la estabilidad del tamaño del efecto no puede verificarse de forma independiente y un único ensayo grande no reportado podría cambiar materialmente las estimaciones agrupadas.

concerns.issue: Estudios en animales dominan el resultado inflamatorio
concerns.detail: El resultado de inflamación (calificado como Fuerte) incluye 22 de 38 estudios (58%) en modelos animales, pero el efecto agrupado [-0.45 IC: -0.67 a -0.24] se presenta como apoyo a la utilidad clínica humana. Los modelos animales de inflamación a menudo muestran tamaños de efecto mayores que los ensayos humanos; los 16 estudios humanos solos pueden no apoyar la misma solidez de inferencia extraída del conjunto combinado.

El resultado cardiovascular (grado Fuerte) agrupa estudios sobre miopatía inducida por estatinas, estrés cardíaco en atletas, pacientes quemados, prediabetes, rendimiento del ejercicio y perfiles de lípidos—fisiopatologías y puntos finales distintos. La diferencia de media agrupada de -0.96 [-1.88 a -0.03] tiene un IC del 95% que apenas excluye cero y se calcula en escenarios clínicos fundamentalmente incomparables, lo que genera dudas sobre si la estimación agrupada refleja alguna afirmación clínica única y accionable.

concerns.issue: Colesterol/lípidos calificados como Moderados con evidencia mínima
concerns.detail: Solo 8 estudios totales con 3 reportando tamaños de muestra (n=30, 104, 2794); el metanálisis de 2794 participantes aparece listado pero ningún efecto agrupado es extraíble de los resúmenes proporcionados. El motor nota explícitamente que este resultado está 'por debajo del umbral para el nivel superior' debido a evidencia humana limitada, pero cardiovascular recibe una calificación Fuerte a pesar de poblaciones superpuestas y limitaciones metodológicas similares.

concerns.issue: La evidencia de fuerza muscular es pequeña y fragmentada
concerns.detail: Ocho de 24 estudios de fuerza muscular reportan tamaños de muestra; seis de esos ocho inscribieron ≤38 participantes, y el más grande (n=120) es de 2015. Ninguna conclusión de metanálisis se replica de forma independiente (solo una revisión sistemática única). La mediana de n en los estudios reportados es 25, lo que significa que los intervalos de confianza son amplios y la heterogeneidad del sesgo de ensayos pequeños es plausible.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: CoQ10 es un cofactor bien establecido del transporte de electrones mitocondrial, y la evidencia in vitro respalda funciones en el estrés oxidativo y la inflamación. Sin embargo, la evidencia recuperada no aborda adecuadamente la biodisponibilidad sistémica o la penetración tisular—el ensayo de biodisponibilidad de 2020 está incluido pero sus hallazgos no se sintetizan en afirmaciones sobre si CoQ10 oral alcanza el corazón o el músculo en concentraciones terapéuticas. El salto de la reducción de biomarcadores (PCR, TNF-α, índices de lípidos) a la mejora clínicamente significativa en eventos cardiovasculares o fuerza muscular funcional es sustancial y no se cubre con datos mecanísticos en estos registros.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que cinco de los seis ensayos cardiovasculares aleatorizados (2018–2025) son recientes e incluyen heterogeneidad sustancial en poblaciones y dosis; los metanálisis antiguos y estudios observacionales pueden reflejar sesgo de publicación o enmascaramiento inadecuado. El resultado de inflamación, calificado como Fuerte, está impulsado por un consenso de 5 metanálisis, pero cuatro de cinco metanálisis son de 2017–2023 e incluyen explícitamente datos animales; si el subconjunto solo humano muestra inconsistencia o tamaños de efecto menores, la afirmación de replicación adecuadamente potenciada se desmorona. Lo más crítico es que el efecto cardiovascular agrupado es -0.96 con un IC que abarca cero a -1.88—si se interpreta de forma conservadora, el límite inferior es clínicamente trivial (−0.03), y la estimación puntual podría ser fácilmente ruido en un metanálisis de ensayos pequeños.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo aleatorizado grande (n≥500), adecuadamente potenciado con un resultado clínico preespecificado (p. ej., reducción de eventos cardiovasculares, función muscular por medidas estandarizadas en una única población de enfermedad) y reporte explícito de enmascaramiento, ocultación de asignación y desgaste establecería si las mejoras de biomarcadores se traducen en beneficio relevante para el paciente. Alternativamente, una revisión sistemática que agrupe por separado solo ensayos aleatorizados humanos, estratifique por población y resultado, y cuantifique la heterogeneidad aclararía si las calificaciones Fuertes se apoyan únicamente en evidencia humana o se inflan por datos animales.
